blocks.text: Profiling and optimization help improve the speed and efficiency of a program. Profiling measures how much time and resources each part of the code uses. Optimization focuses on making slow or resource-heavy parts faster. These techniques are important for building high-performance applications. Regular profiling ensures that code remains efficient as it grows.

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text: Profiling helps identify slow parts of a program so they can be improved for better performance.
The following code shows a nested loop:
In this code, the outer loop runs 10,000 times. For every single iteration of the outer loop, the inner loop also runs 10,000 times. Therefore, the total number of executions becomes:

This means the inner statement may run one hundred million times, which can make the program very slow. Such a part of the code is called a performance bottleneck. Profiling tools help programmers identify these slow sections so that they can optimise the code and improve program efficiency.

Profiling tools track the execution time and memory usage of different functions in a program. Python provides modules like cProfile and timeit for this purpose. These tools generate reports showing which parts of the code are slow or resource-intensive (as shown in Figure 5.3). Measuring performance helps prioritize areas for optimization.

Performance bottlenecks are sections of code that slow down the program. Profiling reports help locate these bottlenecks. Optimization techniques include improving algorithms, reducing unnecessary operations, or using efficient data structures. Fixing bottlenecks improves overall program speed and responsiveness (as shown in Figure 5.4).

blocks.text:
import cProfile
import timeit


# Slow code example
def slow_sum(numbers):
    total = 0

    # Adding numbers one by one using a loop
    for num in numbers:
        total = total + num

    return total


# Fast code example
def fast_sum(numbers):
    # Python built-in sum() is faster and optimised
    return sum(numbers)


# Main function
def main():
    numbers = list(range(1, 1000000))

    print("Slow code result:", slow_sum(numbers))
    print("Fast code result:", fast_sum(numbers))


# Profiling the program using cProfile
print("Profiling Report:")
cProfile.run("main()")


# Comparing execution time using timeit
numbers = list(range(1, 1000000))

slow_time = timeit.timeit(lambda: slow_sum(numbers), number=10)
fast_time = timeit.timeit(lambda: fast_sum(numbers), number=10)

print("\nTime Comparison Report:")
print("Slow code time:", slow_time)
print("Fast code time:", fast_time)

items: cProfile generates a profiling report that shows how much time each function takes during program execution.
slow_sum() is slower because it adds numbers manually using a loop.
fast_sum() is faster because it uses Python's built-in sum() function, which is already optimised.
The function taking more execution time is called the bottleneck.
timeit helps compare the execution time of slow and fast code.

fast_sum() takes less time because it uses Python's built-in sum() function.
Therefore, slow_sum() is the bottleneck in this program.
